title: Lower-bound characterization of communication complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function, let $D(f) \in \bbn_\infty$ denote its deterministic communication complexity, and let $n$ be a natural number. Then $n \le D(f)$ if and only if every deterministic protocol $p$ that computes $f$ has communication complexity at least $n$.
hypotheses_covered: f : X → Y → α is the target function
biconditional: n ≤ D(f) iff every protocol computing f has complexity ≥ n
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and $n : \mathbb{N}$, we have $n \le D(f)$ (in
$\mathbb{N}_\infty$) if and only if every protocol $p : \mathrm{Protocol}\;X\;Y\;\alpha$
that computes $f$ satisfies $n \le p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
